Priya Nair: Quick note from the model bring-up farm: the q4-int8 variant (redwood-econ-7b-q4) passes our unitized short-context checks but fails continuity in the long-window harness past ~66k tokens.
Marco Ruiz: hm. Is that a RoPE amplitude scaling effect or the kernel's index arithmetic?
Priya Nair: Initial signal looks like a phase discontinuity in attention scores when position ids exceed 65536. Repro script:```
./tools/long_context_eval --model builds/redwood-econ-7b-q4 --prompt longsets/seq_70k.txt --track-attn --seed 7 --save-dump out/70k-dump.npz
```
Priya Nair: Key snippet from attention diagnostics:```
LAYER 10: max(attn_phase_diff) @pos=65535->65536 = 3.14e-1
LAYER 10: qkv_idx_written=65536, qkv_idx_read=-1 (masked)
LAYER 10: attn_weights sum deviation=0.12 (expected < 1e-3)
```
Tess B.: Negative read index? That smells like signed overflow when storing position in a 16-bit field. But our cache uses 48-bit offsets elsewhere.
Noah Green: The quant pipeline for q4-int8 introduced a compact meta header to save SRAM for cache meta. We used int16 for token offsets to halve header size. Oops.
Marco Ruiz: Can we repro on fp16 or the q8h path to confirm the header is the culprit?
Priya Nair: fp16: green. q8h: green. q4-int8: failing. So path-specific.
eng-ci-bot: CI job started: eng-ml/long-window/4987654322 -> queued
Noah Green: Repro narrowed: toggling rotary_scale to 0.5 changes where the discontinuity appears (earlier vs later), which suggests RoPE index multiplication crosses a signed boundary in the compact header.
Priya Nair: I instrumented the cache header for a single run with verbose prints:```
struct kv_meta { int16_t pos_lo; uint32_t shard; } // compact header
// write pos=65536 -> pos_lo = -32768
```
Priya Nair: So pos_lo wraps. The read path uses sign-extend and reconstructs a negative offset -> read fails.
Marco Ruiz: Two-pronged fix: (1) short term: change compact header to uint32_t pos_lo for canary builds; (2) longer term: design a variable-width header that uses 3 bytes for >16-bit positions. Add checks in kernel that assert no wrap.
Tess B.: Also add an onboarding checklist item: "does new quant kernel assume header width < needed position range?" and include an automated test that runs with simulated very long priming (>= 100k tokens).
Noah Green: I'll open ENG-ML-7310: "q4-int8 compact header overflow for long-context RoPE" with repro and suggested mitigation.
Priya Nair: Proposed temporary workaround: runtime config 'kv.meta_mode=wide' to opt-in 32-bit positions on Dedicated and Private. We can flip routing to avoid q4-int8 for customers with predicted long-prefix behavior until root cause shipped.
eng-ci-bot: CI job update: eng-ml/long-window/4987654322 -> in_progress
Marco Ruiz: Also need to verify off-by-one interplay with continuous-batching. If batch merges requests, absolute position numbers can spike unexpectedly. Add a fuzz harness that simulates merged prefixes at random offsets.
Priya Nair: Agreed. I added a small fuzz:```
for i in range(100):
  merge_offsets = random.choice([0, 32000, 65500, 70000])
  run_merge_test(offset=merge_offsets)
```
Priya Nair: Fuzz found a second class of failure where merging two 40k prefixes into a 80k effective offset triggers the same header wrap.
Tess B.: Good catch. That means routing avoidance alone is brittle. We must fix metadata width or add explicit overflow guards in the pack/unpack functions.
Noah Green: Patch plan: keep compact header default but compile-time guard to promote header to 32-bit when ROTARY_SCALE != 1.0 or when model.max_context > 65536. Also add unit test: assert(pack(unpack(x)) == x) for x in [0..131072].
Marco Ruiz: Add regression eval: BLEU and perplexity runs on our 70k validation set comparing q4-int8 vs fp16 to ensure we don't get silent quality regressions post-fix.
Priya Nair: I ran a quick perplexity snapshot: q4-int8 (broken) => PPL +14% vs fp16; q4-int8 (with wide-header) => PPL +1.2% (acceptable). Will attach results to ticket.
eng-ci-bot: CI job completed: eng-ml/long-window/4987654322 -> failed (repro confirmed)
Priya Nair: Thanks team. I'll land the emergency wide-header canary patch, add the fuzz harness, and schedule a rollout plan. Tagging this for tomorrow's kernel triage.
Marco Ruiz: Thx. Please add a short note to the onboarding doc so new quant kernels run the long-window header sanity check before merge.
Priya Nair: Will do.
